channels.credentials: Matt Casturo, DPT (Doctor of Physical Therapy), CSCS (NSCA Certified Strength & Conditioning Specialist); former collegiate/high school S&C coach and founder of The Movement System CSCS education platform.
channels.why: Top pick #1. Highest pedagogical clarity and direct citation of peer-reviewed literature and NSCA CSCS 5th-edition guidelines on YouTube. Explains plyometric ground-contact volume dosing, SSC mechanics (<250ms vs >250ms), 5-level landing/plyo progressions, force-plate CMJ/RSI diagnostics, RFD, and tendon mechanotransduction (≥70% MVIC strain rule, HSR vs isometrics) in concise 6-18 minute structured lectures with zero clickbait.

channels.credentials: Paul Fabritz, B.S. Kinesiology, CSCS; NBA & pro basketball performance specialist (trainer to James Harden, Joel Embiid, Buddy Hield, Mac McClung) and creator of The Vert Code & The Durability Code.
channels.why: Top pick #2. Best bridge between peer-reviewed tendon/biomechanics science (citing Keith Baar, Jill Cook, Andy Galpin, Jake Tuura) and basketball-specific vertical jump programming. Unmatched on 1-foot vs 2-foot approach jump mechanics (penultimate step, block foot), standing-vs-approach deficit testing, 'tendon jerk budget' management, jump frequency myths (72-hour collagen synthesis), and low-impact explosive training for older/cranky basketball knees.

channels.credentials: Jake Tuura, M.S. Exercise Science, CSCS; ~10 years NCAA collegiate S&C coach (Youngstown State, Westminster), founder of Jacked Athlete, creator of Jumper's Knee Protocol and Vertical Jump Protocol.
channels.why: Gold-standard clinical/research depth on patellar and Achilles tendinopathy (citing Jill Cook, Karin Silbernagel, Keith Baar, Falk Mersmann), 24-hour pain-response autoregulation ('pain tomorrow matters more than pain in training'), heavy slow resistance (HSR), and return-to-jumping progressions. Note: his brand is Jacked Athlete (not 'Project Next'). Excluded from top 2 only because his short-form videos are hyper-focused on tendon rehab snippets (2-4 min) and his newer uploads are 60-100 min researcher interviews rather than unified jump programming lectures.

channels.candidateEvaluated: Matt McInnes Watson (Plus Plyos / The Plyo Guy)
channels.credentials: Matt McInnes Watson, MSc Sports Performance, BSc Physical Therapy, UKSCA Accredited S&C Coach; former track & field high jumper and founder of Plus Plyos.
channels.why: Exceptional systematic framework for plyometric dosing via a 4-tier continuum (Light/Extensive, Medium, Deep, and Shock tiers), ground-contact-time progression, landing stiffness, and Achilles/knee load management. Slightly narrower on heavy barbell strength integration and basketball approach-jump biomechanics than the Movement System + PJF pairing.

channels.credentials: Joel Smith, M.S. Exercise Science, CSCS; former NCAA DI Track & Field / S&C coach (UC Berkeley, Wilmington College), author of Vertical Foundations and Speed Strength, host of Just Fly Performance Podcast.
channels.why: Deeply knowledgeable DI sprints/jumps coach who hosts top sport scientists (Dr. Keith Baar, Cal Dietz, Jake Tuura, Vern Gambetta). Ranked 4/5 for corpus extraction because most channel uploads are 60-90 minute conversational podcast interviews (including some esoteric fascia/oscillatory topics) rather than concise, structured programming breakdowns.

channels.candidateEvaluated: The Max Schmarzo Project (Strong by Science)
channels.credentials: Max Schmarzo, M.S. Kinesiology / Applied Sport Science, CSCS; Chief Science Officer at Resilience Code, NBA/pro basketball sport scientist and author of Applied Principles of Optimal Power Development.
channels.why: Elite applied sport scientist on force-velocity profiling, RFD, and isometric/dynamic CNS profiling, plus relatable recent vlogs as a 32-33 year old dad rebuilding basketball athleticism around injuries. Ranked 4/5 because recent channel content is primarily personal basketball tournament/training vlogs rather than structured educational lectures.

channels.credentials: John Evans, M.S. Exercise Physiology, CSCS; co-founder of THP Strength and coach to world-record vertical jumpers Isaiah Rivera (50.5") and Dillan McCarthy (51").
channels.why: The scientific brain behind THP Strength. Explains Bondarchuk/conjugate periodization, motor unit recruitment, tendon stiffness vs compliance, and squat-to-bodyweight thresholds for 40"+ jumpers using athlete tracking data. Ranked 4/5 because video titles use high-clickbait YouTube packaging and programming targets 20-something max-effort dunk specialists more than late-30s recreational basketball players.

channels.credentials: Co-hosted by John Evans (M.S. Exercise Physiology, CSCS) and Isaiah Rivera (50.5" verified approach vertical jump, pro dunker).
channels.why: Daily podcast/screen-share channel of THP Strength covering conjugate jump blocks, power cleans vs trap-bar jumps, sprinting vs jumping volume trade-offs, and case studies (including late-30s jumpers). High practical value from coaching elite dunkers, though conversational and mixed with clickbait titles.

channels.credentials: Pro dunker with a verified 50.5" max approach vertical jump; co-founder of THP Strength (note: 'Rebound Plus' is not his brand; likely conflated with THP Strength / Plus Plyos).
channels.why: Elite practitioner on approach jump mechanics (penultimate step, plant angles, arm swing) and practical dunk session structure, backed by co-founder John Evans's exercise physiology principles. Ranked 3/5 because his personal channel mixes solid technique/training advice with viral dunk exhibitions, reaction videos, and 'Jump Higher in 5 Minutes' clickbait titles.

channels.credentials: Founded by Owen Walker, MSc Sport Science (former Head of Academy Sport Science, Cardiff City FC); staffed by MSc/PhD sport scientists and CSCS/UKSCA coaches.
channels.why: Peer-reviewed, textbook-accurate sport science platform covering force-velocity curves, RFD, RSI, supercompensation, and plyometric mechanics. Ranked 4/5 for this task because YouTube uploads are mostly 2-4 minute animated glossary summaries or general S&C podcast clips with limited depth on vertical-jump-specific weekly programming.

channels.credentials: Founded by Dr. Marcus Elliott, MD (Harvard Medical School) and led by Eric Leidersdorf, M.S. Biomechanics; premier NBA biomechanics and force-plate assessment lab (has assessed >60% of NBA players).
channels.why: World-class 3D motion-capture and dual-force-plate laboratory in Santa Barbara, CA, but their official YouTube channel contains only 7 short promotional/athlete-feature videos (2016-2019) and zero instructional programming lectures. P3's research insights are only accessible via third-party podcast appearances or peer-reviewed papers.

channels.channelName: Coach Chris Korfist (Slow Guy Speed School)
channels.credentials: Chris Korfist, M.S. Education; 30+ year sprint coach (Hinsdale Central / Homewood-Flossmoor HS), owner of Slow Guy Speed School, co-founder of Track Football Consortium and Reflexive Performance Reset (RPR).
channels.why: Innovative sprint/ankle-rocker specialist using 1080 Sprint force-velocity data and foot/ankle stiffness drills, but primarily focused on linear sprinting rather than basketball vertical jump programming. Frequently relies on proprietary neurological heuristics (RPR) rather than peer-reviewed jump literature.

channels.credentials: None verified in S&C or sport science (Australian aerobatic/stunt pilot; name appears to be a prompt conflation, possibly with NZ sport scientist Dr. Hayden Pritchard, PhD, CSCS, who does not run a vertical jump YouTube channel).
channels.why: Verified via YouTube Data API v3 and Google Search: no vertical jump or strength & conditioning coach named Hayden Pullen exists on YouTube. The channel matching this exact name has 14 subscribers and 3 personal videos.

channels.credentials: None verified in vertical jump S&C on YouTube (name appears to be a prompt conflation with Dr. Matt Casturo, DPT, CSCS of The Movement System or Matt McInnes Watson, MSc, PT of Plus Plyos).
channels.why: Verified via YouTube Data API v3 and Google Search: no credentialed vertical jump / plyometrics YouTube channel exists under 'Matt Ritchie' (only a 1-subscriber personal account and clips of pro footballer Matt Ritchie). Evaluated and replaced in top picks by Dr. Matt Casturo (The Movement System) and Matt McInnes Watson (Plus Plyos).

videos.title: A Coaches Guide to Plyometric Training
videos.principle: Explains the stretch-shortening cycle (SSC), fast (<250ms) vs slow (>250ms) ground contact times, amortization efficiency, and how to match plyometric drill intensity and rest periods to specific RFD and reactive-strength adaptations.

videos.title: New CSCS Guidelines for Plyometric Training Volume (5th Edition Update)
videos.principle: Details the updated NSCA CSCS 5th-edition plyometric volume guidelines (ground contacts per session and per week by training age) and how to scale contact dose inversely with drill intensity.

videos.title: How to Progress Plyometrics | 5 Levels From Beginner to Advanced
videos.principle: Establishes a 5-level plyometric progression gate (stick landings -> stabilization hops -> submaximal rhythmic hops -> maximal jumps -> depth/shock jumps) so athletes earn high-impact readiness without knee overload.

videos.title: Force Plate Testing for Vertical Jump | 5 Numbers You Need to Know
videos.principle: Breaks down the 5 key force-plate vertical jump metrics (jump height, RSI, eccentric RFD, concentric impulse, and force-velocity deficit) used to diagnose whether an athlete needs more maximal strength or more reactive plyometrics.

videos.title: Vertical Jump Training Program | Jump HIGHER with SCIENCE
videos.principle: Demonstrates a 3-phase periodized vertical jump program (hypertrophy/eccentric base -> maximal strength -> RFD/power/contrast + plyometric peaking) balancing barbell loads with jump volume across the week.

videos.title: The Complete Guide to Tendon Training for Athletes
videos.principle: Synthesizes peer-reviewed tendon adaptation science (the >=70% MVIC strain threshold for collagen crosslinking/stiffness, why light high-rep work fails to stiffen tendons, and how to combine heavy slow resistance/isometrics with plyometrics).

videos.title: 008: Jump Mechanics- Fastest Way to Improve Your Vertical Jump- The PJF Podcast
videos.principle: Provides a complete biomechanical breakdown of standing vertical jump vs 2-foot approach jump vs 1-foot approach jump mechanics (penultimate step length, block-foot plant angle, horizontal-to-vertical momentum conversion, and hip vs knee dominance).

videos.title: The Vertical Jump Test You NEED TO DO
videos.principle: Teaches the standing-vs-approach vertical jump differential field test to classify an athlete as elastic-dominant vs strength-dominant and prescribe the right ratio of weight-room strength vs plyometric work.

videos.title: How To Jump Higher WITHOUT Getting Injured (Understanding Tendon Jerk Budget)
videos.principle: Introduces the 'tendon jerk budget' framework—accounting for high-rate-of-force impact spikes from pickup basketball and reactive plyometrics so weekly programming stays below the patellar/Achilles injury threshold.

videos.title: How Often Can We Jump Without Injuring Tendons (72 Hour Myth EXPOSED)
videos.principle: Clarifies jump training frequency and tendon recovery timelines (explaining net collagen synthesis vs degradation curves across 24-72 hours and how to space high-intensity jump sessions vs low-impact microdoses).

videos.title: How to Train the Tendons to Avoid Jumpers Knee and Improve Vertical Jump
videos.principle: Outlines an evidence-based patellar tendinopathy ('jumper's knee') prevention and rehab protocol combining Keith Baar-style 30-45s analgesic isometrics, heavy slow resistance (HSR), and progressive tendon loading.

videos.title: 2 Ways to Train for Explosiveness While Decreasing Impact on the Knees
videos.principle: Shows how a recreational/aging basketball player with cranky knees can maintain high concentric rate of force development and jump power using reduced-landing-force substitutions (box/sled/band-resisted power work) when readiness is low.
